_why: Per-chunk gzipped budgets, checked by scripts/check-bundle-budget.mjs after a build. Lighthouse audits pages and so counts only what /login and /consortium/insights fetch; this reaches every chunk, including the ones no audited page touches. Numbers are what each chunk measured when the budget was added, plus 2% rounded up - enough that an ordinary edit does not fail the build, not enough to absorb a new dependency. Never raise one to make a build pass: docs/performance-budget.md.

_notes.totalBytes: 1,652,603 bytes gzipped across 384 chunks, measured 2026-10-07 on a VITE_PUBLIC_URL=/ build. For comparison on the same date: dcb-admin-for-libraries budgets 1,252,000 and the discovery UI 1,040,000. This application ships MUI X Premium's grid, charts AND pickers where those ship one grid, which is most of the difference - and is the number to aim at rather than to declare.
_notes.exceljs.min.js: MUI X Premium's Excel export, a direct dependency of @mui/x-data-grid-premium, and 17% of everything this application ships. It was dead weight until the export menu began offering Excel (docs/mappings-export.md); it leaves entirely on DataGridPro, which is worth measuring against what Premium features the grids actually use. Both sibling repos record the same chunk and the same question.
_notes.DataGrid.js: The Premium grid itself, on fifty mount sites.
_notes.BarChartPro.js: x-charts-pro, reached only from Insights. Raised from 107500 to 110000 on 2026-10-08, re-derived from 107753 measured: +253 gzipped, 0.24%, for MUI X 9.13.0 -> 9.15.0. Two minor releases of a dependency this repository does not control and cannot bump alone - MUI X is pinned in lockstep with dcb-admin-for-libraries - so this is upstream drift rather than anything the application added. The previous number was measured+2% and two minors ate it. Still a candidate for React.lazy on the chart panels, which would move the chunk off the Insights critical path rather than shrink it.
_notes.rasterizeHTML.js: Pulled in by the grid's print export. Not obviously load-bearing - worth checking whether print is reachable at all.
_notes.i18n.js: The translation catalogue. i18n-unused reports 952 of 2,638 keys unused, ~34.5 KB, so this chunk is carrying about a third more than it needs to.
_notes.Stack.js: @mui/material, named after whichever module anchors the chunk. A rename shows up here as one chunk unbudgeted and another no longer built, which is noisy but not wrong.
_notes.useThemeStore.css: The application's stylesheet, including the @font-face rules. The name is the bundler's, derived from the module that anchors the chunk.
_notes.axios.js: Raised from 17200 to 19000 on 2026-10-08, re-derived from 18591 measured: +1391 gzipped for axios 1.18.1 -> 1.20.0. That bump closes twelve advisories, and the four that matter in a browser are header injection via inherited headers and the prototype-pollution gadgets in the fetch adapter and toFormData - on the client that carries the bearer token to dcb-service. 1.4 KB for that is not a trade worth arguing about. The Node-adapter advisories in the same release (HTTP/2, NO_PROXY, createConnection) are not reachable from a browser and are not the reason.
